summary: This Wikipedia-derived note covers the late 17th-century effort by the English crown to reorganize New England, culminating in the Dominion of New England under Sir Edmund Andros. It describes how Andros's rule was unpopular, how the 1689 Boston revolt overthrew him, and how he was imprisoned, escaped, and was later acquitted in England.
one_line: Account of the 1689 Boston revolt against Sir Edmund Andros and the Dominion of New England, and Andros's imprisonment and acquittal.
key_facts: King Charles II of England began reorganizing the New England colonies in the early 1680s.
The charter of the Massachusetts Bay Colony was revoked in 1684 after its leaders refused to act on Charles II's demands for reforms.
Roman Catholic James II, Charles II's successor, continued the reorganization and created the Dominion of New England.
James II appointed former New York governor Sir Edmund Andros as dominion governor in 1686.
In 1688, the Dominion of New England's jurisdiction was expanded to include New York, East Jersey, and West Jersey.
Andros disregarded local representation, denied the validity of existing Massachusetts land titles, and restricted town meetings.
Andros enforced the Navigation Acts, which threatened the existence of certain New England trading practices.
Fort Mary surrendered on the 19th, and Andros was moved there from Usher's house.
Andros was transferred to Castle Island on June 7 after being confined with Joseph Dudley and other dominion officials.
Robert Ratcliff, Boston's Anglican minister, called stories of Andros escaping in women's clothing "falsehoods and lies" meant to "render the Governour odious to his people".
Andros escaped from Castle Island on August 2 after his servant bribed the sentries with liquor.
After fleeing to Rhode Island, Andros was recaptured soon after and kept in what was virtually solitary confinement.
Andros and others arrested after the revolt were held for 10 months before being sent to England for trial.
Massachusetts agents in London refused to sign the charge documents against Andros, so he was summarily acquitted and released.
Andros later served as governor of Virginia and Maryland.
